To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the majority of frequently altered genes in BC are transcription factors or their upstream regulators, (ii) alterations in TFs are not random, (iii) the majority of TF alterations in BC affect transcriptional coactivators, and (iv) alterations in TF pathways in BC are associated with the establishment of superenhancers and positive transcription elongation.

In summary, our research is concerned with

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

transcriptional alterations in breast cancer are not restricted to the canonical oncogenic transcriptional program (MYC, E2F1), which is activated in the majority of breast tumors, but also affect other oncogenic transcriptional programs (e.g., TP53, NOTCH, HIPPO, and WNT).
the majority of the transcriptional alterations in BC are not in DB-TFs, but in their cofactors and upstream regulatory factors.
transcriptional regulation of oncogenic signaling pathways is a major mechanism of oncogenesis in breast cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the majority of oncogenic alterations in transcription in BC involve loss of repressive factors or gain of activating factors, which results in aberrant activation of oncogenic transcription.
the transcriptional network is altered at many levels in BC and that the alterations are diverse and complex.
breast cancer cells have evolved multiple mechanisms to induce oncogenic TFs and to rewire the transcriptional network.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the loss of default repressor TFs (e.g., corepressors and upstream factors) may be an important mechanism for oncogenic transcription in breast cancer.
the loss of corepressors, coactivators, and epigenetic modifiers that mediate oncogenic transcriptional repression is more frequent in breast cancer than the loss of oncogenic TFs.
the transcriptional circuitry is a major determinant of breast cancer phenotype.
